app.name: OpenGrid Hub
app.tagline: Publish a model. Test an assumption. Find the data behind both.
app.description: A registry for grid data, assumptions and models. It holds what is registered with it, points at what is already hosted well elsewhere, and says which is which.

nav.signOutFailed: Sign-out failed — you are still signed in. Try again.

studies.title: Studies & Assumptions
studies.blurb: Filings, papers and the interventions that contest them — each with the assumption set it stands on, frozen at a version somebody can cite.

referenceModels.title: Reference Models
referenceModels.blurb: Networks to start from when you have none. Pick a geography; each model declares what class of question it is good for and what it is not.
referenceModels.allPlaces: All {count, plural, one {# geography} other {# geographies}}
referenceModels.notBuiltHere: These are the geographies the Hub has built a reference network for. A place that is not listed is one nobody has built here — not a finding that no such network exists. That claim belongs to the gap register, which records who observed it and when.
referenceModels.unknownPlace: No geography called “{place}” is published here, so every geography is shown.
referenceModels.unplacedHelp: These models do not name a place, so the picker cannot file them. Listed rather than hidden: a record the catalog cannot place is a gap in the record, not a network that is nowhere.

datasets.title: Data Catalog
datasets.blurb: Datasets for power-system modelling, graded on provenance, documentation and currency, with the studies that used them.

custody.body: An object registered here — a model, an assumption set, a study, a reference network — is one the Hub promises will not move, so the Hub holds the bytes. A catalogued dataset is a description of something somebody else promises, so the Hub points at it and never proxies it. Custody, not size, decides which: a four-terabyte reanalysis archive is free to describe.

gapsMoved.title: The gap register moved
gapsMoved.blurb: It is in the catalog now, beside the domain each entry concerns — where a reader meets it while deciding whether this catalog can answer their question, rather than in a section they would have had to go looking for. Every entry still carries who observed it and when.

home.browseAll: Browse all {total, plural, one {# record} other {# records}} →

referenceModel.partition: What this network is rated for
referenceModel.noPartition: No question-class partition recorded for this model yet. That is a gap in the record, not a judgement about the network.
referenceModel.noBasis: No basis recorded for this claim.
referenceModel.shareAlikeHelp: This model's licence obliges derived works to carry the same terms. ODbL share-alike operates at the database level, so joining it to your own data may bring that data into scope — an open question for adopters, not a settled one. Read the licence before you build on it.

networkMap.alt: Map of {name}: transmission network on a real coastline.
networkMap.unavailable: The network could not be loaded.
networkMap.unavailableHelp: This is a failure to read the model file, not a statement that the model is empty.
networkMap.navigationHelp: Drag to pan, or focus the map and use the arrow keys. Use + and − to zoom, and Home to reset. Shift with ← and → steps through the network's components, and Page Up and Page Down move through them twenty-five at a time.
networkMap.identifyHelp: Point at a bus or a circuit to name it. On a keyboard, focus the map and hold Shift with ← and → to step through its components; on a touchscreen, tap one.

modelPage.title: {model}: the model document
modelPage.blurb: Every component the registered document carries, with the value basis the record declares for each field and, where a value was estimated, the rule and the inputs behind it. The file is still the file — this is what it says.
modelPage.unavailable: The model document could not be read.
modelPage.unavailableHelp: This is a failure to fetch the file, not a statement that the model is empty. The record and its download are unaffected.
modelPage.noFields: This record declares no component fields.
modelPage.noFieldsHelp: The table is built from the record's field declarations, which say where in the document each value lives and on what basis it was set. Without them there is nothing here that could be labelled honestly, and an unlabelled dump of the file is what this page exists instead of.
modelPage.componentsHelp: One table per component type the record describes. The basis under each column heading is the record's own — measured, estimated or modeled — and a column with a caveat carries it on the heading.
modelPage.filterPlaceholder: Filter by component name or upstream id
modelPage.caption: Components of type {kind}, with their recorded values.

search.label: Search the catalog
search.resultsCount: {count, plural, =0 {No datasets} one {1 dataset} other {# datasets}}
search.typing: Results update as you type. There is no submit step.
search.catalogUnavailable: The full catalog could not be loaded. Search results are unavailable until it can be read.
search.previewCount: Preview · {count, plural, one {1 dataset} other {# datasets}}
search.previewHelp: These are the initial catalog entries. Search results and the full count will appear once the catalog loads.
search.unsupportedTitle: This filter is not available in the static catalog
search.unsupportedHelp: Unsupported filters: {filters}. Clear them to search this catalog.
search.searchingHelp: Results for a search or a filter need the whole catalog, so none are shown until it loads. The entries that shipped with this page are the first page of the catalog, not an answer to this query.

empty.noResultsHelp: The catalog holds {total} datasets. Try removing a filter, or searching for the quantity you need rather than the dataset's name. ERA5's column {column} resolves to the concept {concept} — search for the concept and you find every dataset that carries the quantity, whatever each one calls its column.
empty.gapHelp: The catalog has no dataset for this, and that is a finding rather than a hole in our coverage:
empty.gapStale: Due for re-checking — this was observed in {year} and may have changed.
empty.notFoundHelp: Either this record does not exist, or it is one whose existence is restricted. The catalog answers both the same way, deliberately: a distinguishable refusal would tell you which.
empty.noDistributions: No access path is recorded for this dataset.
empty.noStudiesHelp: A study is a filing, a paper or an intervention, registered with the assumption set it stands on. Nothing has been registered in this build.
empty.referenceModelsUnavailable: Reference models could not be loaded.
empty.referenceModelsUnavailableHelp: This is a failure to read the catalog, not a statement that no reference model is published. Nothing here has been withdrawn.
empty.noReferenceModelsHelp: A reference model is a network you can start from, carrying a declared fidelity class rather than a README's worth of prose. None is published in this build.
empty.noGapsHelp: A gap is a data requirement with no open supplier. An empty register means none has been recorded, not that none exists.
empty.gapsUnavailable: The gap register could not be loaded.
empty.gapsUnavailableHelp: This is a failure to read the register, not a statement that there are no gaps. Nothing here has been withdrawn.
empty.catalogUnavailableHelp: This build returned no records at all. That is a catalog that could not be read, or one with nothing in it, and this page cannot tell the two apart — so it claims neither. The catalog page reports which.

levelHelp.1: Dataset-level metadata, at least one distribution, licence and coverage. Enough to find it and to get at it.
levelHelp.2: Field names, definitions, types and value basis. Enough to read the schema and to grade provenance and documentation.
levelHelp.3: Concept IRIs, unit IRIs and field sources. Enough for semantic resolution and inter-dataset links.

dataset.referenceOnlyHelp: The catalog records where this dataset is and who publishes it, and does not describe its contents.
dataset.caveatsHelp: What the catalog knows about working with this dataset, including what it does not know.
dataset.lineageDepth: {depth, plural, =0 {Observational — nothing sits between this and a measurement} =1 {One layer of assumptions between this and an observation} other {# layers of assumptions between this and an observation}}
dataset.lineageUnknown: How many layers of assumptions sit under this is not recorded. That is not the same as none.
dataset.fieldsDescribed: {count, plural, one {# field described} other {# fields described}}
dataset.fieldsDescribedHelp: How many of this dataset's fields the catalog can describe. Separate from the completeness level: level 1 means no field metadata by definition, and level 2 additionally requires a definition and a value basis on every field, which a schema probe cannot supply.

overview.exclusionHelp: The exclusions are the half you cannot get anywhere else. A dataset that is wrong for your question is worth knowing about before you build on it.
overview.notCapturedHelp: Absent means this has not been catalogued — never that the dataset lacks it.
overview.usedByHelp: Studies, tutorials and tools recorded as having used this dataset. An empty section means nothing has been recorded — most catalogues have no field that could carry it — not that nobody uses the data.

provenance.upstreamAbsentHelp: Which is a statement about what the catalog can show, not about how the data was produced.
provenance.supersededHelp: Prefer the newer record for new work.

schema.inferredHelp: Drafted by the enricher and not yet confirmed by a steward.
schema.gapHelp: The catalog says why, rather than leaving the cell blank.
schema.filterPlaceholder: Filter fields by name, description, unit or concept
schema.report: Report an issue with this field

quality.title: Three independent facets
quality.help: Graded separately and never combined. A dataset can be perfectly current and completely unprovenanced, and one number would hide exactly that.
quality.notAssessedHelp: Not the same as a poor grade. Provenance and documentation are graded from field-level metadata, which this record does not carry yet.
quality.visibleToAll: Visible without signing in, deliberately: an evaluator comparing catalogs should not have to register first.

connections.title: One hop from this dataset
connections.capHelp: The twelve strongest are shown first.

downloads.title: Access paths
downloads.help: OpenGrid redirects you to the source and never proxies the bytes. For a partial read of a large dataset, use the SDK — it fetches an access plan and reads only the slice you asked for.
downloads.noneTitle: No access path — catalogued so the gap is visible
downloads.noneHelp: OpenGrid lists this dataset without being able to offer it. Knowing that it exists, and why it is out of reach, is more useful than the catalog staying silent about it.
downloads.sdk: Read a slice with the SDK
downloads.healthHelp: Last checked {when}. A path that has failed three consecutive checks is excluded from access plans and a working sibling is substituted.

report.title: Report an issue
report.subtitle: Tell us what is wrong. You do not need an account.
report.emailHelp: Only so we can ask a follow-up question. Leave it blank to report anonymously.
report.thanks: Thank you — the report is with the curation team.
report.failed: That did not send. Please try again.

submit.title: Submit a dataset
submit.subtitle: Suggest a dataset for the catalog. No account needed; we ask for a contact so we can follow up if something is unclear.
submit.contactHelp: So we can ask a question if something is unclear. It is not published.
submit.thanks: Thank you. The submission is in the curation queue.
submit.thanksHelp: We do not track submissions back to submitters, so this is the last you will hear from the form. If we need to ask something, we will email you.
submit.failed: That did not send. Please try again.

connect.title: Connect with AI
connect.subtitle: The catalog speaks MCP, so an assistant can search it, read a record and get an access plan — under your identity, never with more access than you have.
connect.grounding: Every answer is grounded in the catalog. The server has no way to compose a dataset, so it cannot invent one — which matters, because a plausible invented dataset is worse than no answer and you cannot tell them apart.
connect.noData: No tool returns data. They return metadata and access plans; your assistant fetches the data itself.

review.title: Review queue
review.subtitle: Highest leverage first: most inbound links, then most complete. A record twelve others cite is worth an hour before one nothing points at.
review.signIn: Sign in as a steward to see the queue.
review.forbidden: This queue is for stewards. You are signed in as someone else.
review.forbiddenHelp: A 403 rather than a 404, deliberately: the queue's existence is not a secret, only its contents are — so you are told to change sessions rather than sent looking for a typo.
review.emptyHelp: Every harvested record in this state has been reviewed. New ones arrive when a harvest lands.
review.conflictHelp: A re-harvest found the source changing a value under a field a steward had already confirmed. The record is flagged rather than silently overwritten.

static.title: This is a static copy of the catalog.
static.help: These pages were built from a snapshot of the public catalog and are served as files, so there is no service behind them to receive a form or to check who you are. Everything that only reads — search, records, schemas, quality, connections — works exactly as it does on the live site. Anything that writes, or that depends on your identity, needs the live deployment.
static.searchNote: Filtered in your browser over the whole public catalog. The live site ranks results with a real scoring function; this matches on words, so the order is not the same.

signin.title: Sign in
signin.subtitle: Through an identity provider you already have. The Hub holds no passwords, so there is nothing here to register.
signin.browsingIsOpen: Browsing needs none of this. Public records are readable signed out; a session is what the steward queue and personal access tokens require.
signin.unavailableHelp: The API did not respond ({status}). Nothing is wrong with your account — try again shortly.
signin.noneConfiguredHelp: This deployment has no identity provider credentials, so there is nobody to sign in with. Whoever runs it sets DATAHUB_OIDC_PROVIDERS and the matching client id and secret.
signin.restrictedNote: Restricted records you are entitled to are reachable through the API and the SDK with a personal access token. This site reads the catalog anonymously so pages can be cached, so signing in here does not reveal them.

account.title: Your account
account.stewardHelp: Stewards review harvested records before they are published.
account.custodianHelp: A custodian manages who may see a restricted dataset.
account.tokensHelp: Personal access tokens are issued through the API — POST /v1/auth/tokens — and shown once. Only a keyed hash is stored, so there is no way to show one again.
account.unavailable: Your account cannot be shown right now.
account.unavailableHelp: The API did not answer ({status}), so this page cannot say who you are. You have not been signed out — try again in a moment.

catalogCoverage.title: What the catalog holds
catalogCoverage.help: Records by domain and by how well described they are. A thin row means this catalog holds little for that domain — not that little exists. What nobody publishes is a separate claim, and the register entries beside each row are the ones somebody actually made, with their name and the date on them.
catalogCoverage.caption: Catalog records by data domain and completeness level, with gap-register entries per domain.
catalogCoverage.orphanTitle: Entries in domains the catalog holds nothing for
catalogCoverage.orphanHelp: The register's strongest findings, and the ones a table of what the catalog has cannot show.

study.frozenHelp: When the study's inputs stopped moving. A filing is a claim about a moment, and without it a reader cannot tell whether it predates the data it appears to contradict.
study.threadsBlurb: Grouped by docket, so a filing and the interventions contesting it read as one argument rather than four unrelated rows. The grouping comes from what each record declares — nothing here infers that one study answers another.
study.boundToHelp: A study is a set of choices laid over a network somebody else can download and check. This is the network.
study.notInCatalogHelp: Cited by the study, and no record of it is held here. Named rather than linked: dropping the citation would lose the trace, and linking it would promise a page that does not exist.
study.assumptionsBlurb: Every parameter value the study stands on, keyed to where it lands in the model, with what kind of claim it is and where it came from.
study.schemaPinHelp: Two sets pinned to different revisions are not comparable value by value, however alike their paths look.
study.receipt: {errors, plural, =0 {No errors} one {# error} other {# errors}}, {warnings, plural, =0 {no warnings} one {# warning} other {# warnings}}
study.basisHelp: 0.098 asserted and 0.098 measured are different claims. A filing that does not distinguish them cannot be argued with.
study.changedHelp: An inherited value needs no defence. A changed one always does, and this is the argument the record gives for it.
study.runsBlurb: The Hub registers runs. It does not execute them, so the party named here is never the Hub.
study.caseHashHelp: Identifies the document actually solved, rather than the study it belongs to. Two runs of the same study on an edited case are not the same run.
study.noRunsHelp: Nobody has registered an execution of this study here. That is a gap in what has been catalogued, not a statement that it was never run.
study.noAssumptionsHelp: This study names no assumption set, so the values behind it are not traceable here.
study.usedBy: {count, plural, one {# registered study} other {# registered studies}}
study.usedByHelp: Objects in this catalog with an assumption set behind them, unlike the citations on the Connections tab — so this is a count somebody can go and check.
study.usedByNoneHelp: No study registered here stands on this record. Most of the catalog is in that position: registering a study is something a filer does, not something a harvest can find.
study.roleAssumptionSource: Took an assumption value from this record
study.onDatasetHelp: A study has no distributions, no licence and no link health, so it is not shown as a dataset. Its assumptions and runs are on its own page.
